rows.source_ref: PMID 12269969 / doi:10.1046/j.1365-2036.2002.01341.x (Yacyshyn et al. 2002, Aliment Pharmacol Ther 16:1761-1770)
rows.source_table: Abstract (Results), final sentence; full text closed-access - value taken from the PubMed/Europe PMC abstract
rows.notes: Verbatim source sentence: 'The 2-4-h transient post-infusion partial thromboplastin time prolongation values, a class effect of phosphorothioate oligonucleotides, were 18, 21 and 23 s for 250, 300 and 350 mg, respectively.' 250 mg was the fixed dose for patients weighing 36-50 kg (>50 kg patients were randomised to 300 or 350 mg), so this is a weight-band group, not a randomised dose arm. GRADE RATIONALE: coagulation-time change is not a platelet endpoint and the source reports no platelet finding whatsoever, so this carries grade 0 and is_platelet_specific=FALSE - the same convention already used in this dataset for the Crooke 2016 aPTT rows (TMSR109-TMSR132). The grade-0 label here means 'no platelet event observed/reported at this exposure', NOT 'no coagulation effect'; the aPTT effect is real, transient, dose-ordered and explicitly labelled a PS class effect. UNIT AMBIGUITY, FLAGGED NOT RESOLVED: the sentence reads as the magnitude of prolongation in seconds (i.e. +18 s over baseline). It could conceivably be an absolute post-infusion PTT value, but 18 s would sit below a normal aPTT reference range (~25-35 s), which makes the increment reading far more likely. Recorded exactly as printed rather than converted or re-based. effect_vs_control is TBD because this was a single-arm dose-ranging trial with no placebo group and the abstract gives no baseline PTT.

rows.source_ref: PMID:18025536; doi:10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.107.724864
rows.source_table: Abstract (Methods and Results)
rows.notes: Verbatim locus, last sentences of the structured abstract's METHODS AND RESULTS section: 'ARC1779 was generally well tolerated, and no bleeding was observed. Adverse events tended to be minor and not dose related.' Study design from the same section: 'randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in 47 healthy volunteers of doses of ARC1779 from 0.05 to 1.0 mg/kg'. GRADE 0 RATIONALE: the rubric grades bleeding on attribution, and grade 3 requires a haemorrhagic event attributable to thrombocytopenia. Zero haemorrhagic events were observed across the whole dose range, so this is an explicit-zero row, which the schema treats as evidence rather than a missing row. Had bleeding events attributable to a platelet deficit occurred they would have carried grade 3. is_platelet_specific=FALSE deliberately: ARC1779's bleeding liability is ON-TARGET blockade of the vWF A1-GPIb axis (i.e. designed inhibition of platelet adhesion), not thrombocytopenia, so this is flagged as an adjacent-haematology row so that models joining grade to design features can filter it out rather than read it as a thrombocytopenia signal. DOSE BAND: recorded verbatim as the printed range '0.05 to 1.0' mg/kg rather than an invented point dose or midpoint, per the schema's dose-band rule; the abstract gives no per-dose-level breakdown of bleeding. readout_value=0 encodes 'no bleeding was observed' as zero incidence; the paper states this qualitatively and does not print a numerator/denominator or split it by arm, hence effect_vs_control=TBD rather than a fabricated placebo comparison. The 47 subjects include placebo recipients but the abstract does not partition them. exposure_duration=TBD: the abstract does not state infusion duration; the registry (NCT00432770) describes 'intravenous bolus or intravenous bolus followed by continuous infusion' but gives no duration, so nothing numeric is asserted. delivery_method=systemic_dose (IV, per NCT00432770 official title). NO thrombocytopenia or platelet-count row is emitted from this source because the abstract never mentions platelet count or thrombocytopenia - per the no-fabrication policy, a source merely not mentioning platelets is not a grade-0 platelet row.

rows.source_table: Abstract (Results) — 'ARC1779 was well tolerated and safe.'
rows.notes: Adjacent (non-platelet-specific) safety row, flagged is_platelet_specific=FALSE. Qualitative author statement only — the abstract gives no adverse-event table, no bleeding-event count and no platelet-specific AE breakdown, and the full text is paywalled, so no numeric incidence can be recorded (readout_value is the verbatim qualitative claim, not a fabricated number). Grade 0 is justified here rather than being a 'source silent about platelets' row, because this same source DOES report platelet counts under 72 h of continuous exposure and reports them rising, not falling. No bleeding row was created: ARC1779 blocks VWF-GPIbalpha by design, so any bleeding would be on-target antithrombotic pharmacology, and in any case the abstract reports no bleeding events to record.

rows.source_table: Abstract (Results) — 'increased platelet counts from 40 x 10(9)/l (38-58 x 10(9)/l)'
rows.notes: *** DISEASE BASELINE, NOT DRUG-INDUCED — DO NOT ATTRIBUTE THIS GRADE TO ARC1779. *** This is the PRE-DOSE platelet count of three patients whose enrolment criterion was thrombocytopenia from type 2B von Willebrand disease. Graded 3 only because the schema grades control/zero-exposure rows on the band actually observed (40 x10^9/L is <50 x10^9/L), and retained only because it is the comparator denominator that makes the on-treatment row interpretable. dose_or_conc_value is set to '0' so the schema's canonical control-row filter (dose_or_conc_value == '0') removes it from any design-feature-to-grade model. If the assembler prefers not to carry non-drug-caused severe bands at all, this is the row to drop; the on-treatment row is self-contained because its effect_vs_control already carries the 40 -> 146 pair. n=3, median with range.

rows.effect_vs_control: 40 -> 146 x10^9/L median (baseline range 38-58; on-treatment maximum range 107-248)
rows.source_table: Abstract (Results) — 'inhibition of hyperactive VWF rapidly increased platelet counts from 40 x 10(9)/l (38-58 x 10(9)/l) to a maximum of 146 x 10(9)/l (107-248 x 10(9)/l)'
rows.notes: HOW THE ON-TARGET/TOXICITY LINE WAS DRAWN: ARC1779 blocks the VWF A1 domain; in type 2B VWD the mutant VWF is hyperactive and clears platelets, so raising the platelet count IS the intended pharmacodynamic effect. This row is therefore NOT a toxicity signal and must not be read as one. It is retained because it is a human platelet-count measurement under 72 h of continuous systemic exposure (plasma ARC1779 76 ug/ml, range 59-130) in which platelet counts ROSE — i.e. no unintended drug-induced platelet-count fall was observed. Grade 0 = no platelet toxicity signal at the tested exposure. n=3 patients; values are medians with ranges as printed. Full regimen: 0.23 mg/kg IV loading dose then 4 ug/kg/min for 72 h; dose_or_conc_value carries the loading dose only because the infusion rate has no matching unit in the controlled vocabulary. Full text paywalled (Thromb Haemost / Thieme); abstract is the only locus available.

rows.source_table: Results, 'Safety' (final paragraph)
rows.notes: GRADING CALL, stated explicitly: the source says 'One participant ... reported a Grade 3 platelet decline to <100x10^9/L'. Graded 3 on the source's own CTCAE severity label (CTCAE grade 3 thrombocytopenia = 25-50 x10^9/L, i.e. <50, which is the schema grade-3 band). The only NUMBER printed is the '<100' threshold, which alone would map to grade 2 (50-99); the exact nadir is not recoverable from the text, so a curator preferring the printed number over the source's severity label would grade this 2. Flagged rather than silently resolved. Clinically: asymptomatic, no clinical bleeding, onset ~65 days after a single 300 mg dose, reported as resolved. n=159 healthy volunteers total across 4 administration groups. Participants with baseline platelets <140 x10^9/L were EXCLUDED at screening, so this occurred in a subject with normal baseline platelets - which makes it more informative than a low-baseline drift.

rows.exposure_duration: 3 loading doses (days -7, -5, -3) then weekly IV in 4wk cycles
rows.source_table: Abstract, Results + Results 'Safety' ('the most commonly reported AE was platelet count decreased for three (60%) patients in cohort 1')
rows.notes: COHORT 1 = danvatirsen 200 mg MONOTHERAPY, n=5 Japanese patients with advanced solid malignancies, NCT03394144. This is the cleanest danvatirsen monotherapy platelet signal available: platelet count decreased was the SINGLE most common adverse event, causally related to danvatirsen, in 60% of patients. Graded 1 (not higher) because Table 2 records ZERO grade >=3 platelet events in cohort 1 and no dose reductions were required in cohort 1 - so all three events were CTCAE grade 1-2 with no intervention. INCLUSION RATIONALE for the on-target exclusion rule: the paper's Discussion says 'the thrombocytopenia caused by danvatirsen treatment is considered to be associated with the on-target inhibition of STAT3, as a similar effect is observed with Janus kinase inhibitors'. This is on-MECHANISM but it is NOT on-INDICATION - the therapeutic intent is antitumour, and platelet loss is an unwanted toxicity. That is categorically different from the anti-vWF (ARC1779) and anti-FIXa (pegnivacogin) aptamers excluded by the brief, whose whole purpose is to inhibit platelet function. Row therefore INCLUDED, with the mechanism recorded so a modeller can stratify on it. FIRST generation-2.5 (16-nt) compound in this dataset.

rows.source_table: Results, 'Immunogenicity' + Discussion
rows.notes: CRITICAL DISTINCTION, do not conflate: these are ANTI-DRUG antibodies to danvatirsen, NOT anti-platelet antibodies. They are therefore NOT the inotersen-type immune mechanism (antiplatelet IgG causing platelet clearance) that drives the schema's grade-3 immune criterion. Recorded because the two positive samples came from a single cohort-2 patient who ALSO had the grade 3 platelet count decrease, which makes the co-occurrence worth preserving for anyone modelling immune-mediated thrombocytopenia - but the paper explicitly concludes 'the presence of antidanvatirsen antibody did not seem to affect the patient's safety and PK'. thrombocytopenia_grade 3 is carried from the co-reported platelet event in the same patient, NOT inferred from the antibody itself; is_platelet_specific FALSE because the assay measures drug antibodies. That patient's predose danvatirsen plasma concentrations were 37.7, 46.2, 41.1 and 80.4 ng/mL at cycles 1, 2, 3 and 5 - above the cohort geometric means.

rows.source_table: Abstract (Results sentence: "Transient activated partial thromboplastin time prolongation occurred after i.v. infusions and minimally after s.c. injections.")
rows.notes: ADJACENT-HEMATOLOGY FALLBACK ROW, flagged is_platelet_specific=FALSE per the schema. aPTT prolongation is the class-typical PS-ASO coagulation effect and is NOT a platelet finding; it is captured under readout_category=coagulation so the trial's full haematology picture is represented, and a strict platelet-only consumer should filter is_platelet_specific==TRUE. GRADE 0 here means only that THIS endpoint carries no thrombocytopenia signal - it is not an assertion that the trial had no platelet event (it did; see the platelet_count row for the same oligo). Magnitude is TBD: the abstract quantifies nothing ("transient" only). dose band "0.1-6" is transcribed verbatim from the abstract's printed i.v. multiple-dose escalation range "(0.1-6 mg/kg)"; the aPTT statement itself is not resolved to a specific dose level in the abstract, so this is the study's dose range, not a dose at which the effect was localised.

rows.source_table: Abstract (Results sentence: "Transient activated partial thromboplastin time prolongation occurred after i.v. infusions and minimally after s.c. injections.")
rows.notes: ADJACENT-HEMATOLOGY FALLBACK ROW, flagged is_platelet_specific=FALSE; companion to the i.v. aPTT row, split out because the abstract distinguishes the two routes ("minimally after s.c. injections"). Route is encoded in system_model because the delivery_method vocabulary has no separate s.c. term - both routes map to systemic_dose. GRADE 0 refers to this coagulation endpoint carrying no thrombocytopenia signal, not to the trial being platelet-event-free. The word "minimally" is the only magnitude the source gives; no s.c. dose level is printed for this observation, so dose is TBD rather than borrowed from the i.v. band.

rows.source_table: Abstract (Results/tolerability sentence: "Two subjects experienced rash, one a reversible platelet decrease, and mild injection site tenderness was noted.")
rows.notes: HUMAN clinical row — the priority class for this dataset. One subject in the Phase I programme had a platelet decrease explicitly described as reversible. GRADING RATIONALE (non-obvious, please read): the abstract gives NO platelet count, no nadir, no percent decline, no denominator and no route/dose attribution, so the grade rests only on the qualitative descriptors available. Grade 1 is assigned because the event is stated to be reversible, no intervention, dose interruption, dose reduction, bleeding or discontinuation is described, and the paper's own conclusion is that the drug was "generally well tolerated intravenously and subcutaneously". Grade 1 should be treated as a FLOOR, not a confirmed ceiling: if the full text (inaccessible - see extraction_notes) shows a count in the 50-99 x10^9/L band or a dose interruption, this row becomes grade 2, and grade 3 if <50 x10^9/L or antibody-mediated. dose_or_conc_value/unit are TBD rather than the printed 0.1-6 mg/kg i.v. band because the abstract does not say whether the affected subject was in the i.v. escalation or an s.c. cohort - assigning the band would be an invented attribution. readout_unit is n_subjects rather than pct_incidence because the abstract states no total N, so an incidence percentage cannot be computed without fabrication. EXCLUSION LINE: ISIS 104838 targets TNF-alpha mRNA and has no intended antiplatelet or antithrombotic pharmacology, so this platelet decrease is an UNINTENDED effect and is correctly in scope; none of the on-target-antithrombotic exclusion (ARC1779 / pegnivacogin class) applies here.
